From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@quantifylabs.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: sudden 5xx spike + tail latency on inference calls (region us-west)

Connor —

We're seeing a large spike in 5xx responses and end-to-end p95 latency for inference calls routed to the us-west cluster starting ~08:45 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~6% and token throughput dropped by ~40%. Our side hasn't changed traffic patterns; we sent the traces and a small pcap to this email (attached).

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? Critical for our checkout flow — procurement is paused until this stabilizes.

I've included ops@quantifylabs so they see the ticket.

Thanks,
Sam Chen
Head of Platform
Quantify Labs

Attachments: quantify_request_traces_20260225.zip (pcap, logs)

Subject: Re: sudden 5xx spike + tail latency on inference calls (region us-west)

Quick summary from triage so far:
- Telemetry: proxy 5xx spike aligns with a surge of TCP retransmits and SYN retries hitting our regional edge between 08:42–09:05 PT. Client RTTs show sudden 150–300ms hops compared to baseline ~20–30ms.
- Traces: packet captures from Quantify show several mid-path RSTs and a subset of DNS responses that are returning unexpected private IPs.
- Hypothesis: split-horizon DNS or an upstream resolver intermittently returning internal addresses is causing the request to be forwarded into an unintended transit path where NAT/resolution mismatches produce SYN timeouts at our edge proxies.

Action items underway:
1) Neha is validating VPC peering route tables and NAT metrics for us-west.
2) I'm collecting proxy-level logs and token-level error payloads for the window and will share a trimmed set.
3) Connor — recommend we brief Quantify execs with a single consolidated timeline once we confirm path/root cause.

Attachments: redwood-internal-snapshot-logs-connor-20260225.txt (proxy excerpts)

Marissa Cole
SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Chen <sam.chen@quantifylabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden 5xx spike + tail latency on inference calls (region us-west)

Update from network checks:
- VPC peering status: active (no BGP flap history). Route tables look unchanged.
- NAT gateway: connection counts spiked ~3x in the affected window; however capacity metrics did not breach configured thresholds.
- Upstream resolver chain: we observed intermittent NXDOMAIN->private-ip fallbacks from a third-party resolver in Quantify's transit path; engineering on the Quantify side confirmed they had a resolver maintenance window overlapping the incident.

Preliminary conclusion: combination of transient resolver behavior + a suboptimal failover path led to requests being routed through a longer transit route (additional AS hops) and some of those paths hit intermediate firewalls/proxies that were applying connection timeouts aggressively. That produced the elevated handshake failures and 5xx churn.

Next steps I'm running now:
- Pinpoint exact AS hops for the failing request ids and capture traceroutes.
- Recommend short-term mitigation: pin Quantify's traffic to our dedicated peering (if available) or modify routing policy to prefer direct peering for the next 24 hours.

Neha Kapoor
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@quantifylabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden 5xx spike + tail latency on inference calls (region us-west)

Sam —

Thanks to Marissa and Neha for the quick analysis. We have two parallel actions:
A) Immediate mitigation (hours):
- We can route Quantify traffic to the dedicated peering for us-west for the next 24 hours to avoid the transient resolver chain. That will require a short coordination window with your networking team — will you approve the switch?
- We'll also increase proxy handshake timeouts in the affected cluster from 3s -> 6s to reduce SYN-abort failures while we stabilize.

B) Longer-term (days):
- Postmortem to validate upstream resolver SLAs and add resolver health monitoring to our edge.
- Add a routing policy that prefers direct peering for customers with sensitive checkout paths.

Sam — please confirm if Quantify can accept the short peering cutover. If yes, I'll schedule the cutover with your ops and our infra at 16:00 PT today. Vivek, Lauren — looping you in because this is at risk of delaying the QNT renewal (sales/procurement are watching).

Connor

Sam

Cutover complete at 16:23 PT. Summary:
- Traffic pinned to dedicated peering; proxy handshake timeout increased during window.
- Post-cutover metrics (15m): 5xx rate back to baseline (0.28%), p95 latency returned within 5% of previous baseline, throughput recovered.
- We captured traceroutes and resolver logs for a 2-hour window and will upload a postmortem to JIRA-INF-4721 tomorrow.

Next immediate asks:
- Vivek / Lauren: agree we present a short exec note to Quantify leadership summarizing root cause and next steps (postmortem + SLA guardrails)?
- Marissa / Neha: please flag any follow-ups that require product/ops changes so I can include them in the timeline.
